what_it_is: App, API and DDoS security vendor with LLM Firewall and Agentic AI Protection.
identity_note: Radware (radware.com). Scope: LLM Firewall, Agentic AI Protection, MCP Server Protection, Agent Trust Management.

1.reason: Agentic AI Protection discovers approved and shadow agents across SaaS, cloud services and end-user devices.
1.evidence: Continuously monitor risks throughout the agent lifecycle and across SaaS, homegrown and end-user devices.
1.has: Agent and tool discovery, risk graph and agent risk scoring in Agentic AI Protection.
1.lacks: No Kubernetes or on-prem inventory. No cloud misconfiguration or CI/CD checks found.

2.reason: Integrates Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry and Bedrock. MCP Tool Control allows or blocks tools per agent.
2.evidence: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic Claude Code, OpenClaw, N8N
2.has: MCP Server Protection, MCP Tool Control and seven named agent platform integrations.
2.lacks: No agent sandbox. Tool allow lists only, no process, file or egress isolation.

3.reason: Agent Behavioral Protection monitors agent actions and blocks malicious ones. No named SIEM or ITSM connector found.
3.evidence: Maintains runtime monitoring of agent actions and intents, detecting and mitigating malicious activities
3.has: Intent-aware runtime detection and blocking of agent hijack, tool misuse and rogue agents.
3.lacks: No cloud control-plane logs, named SIEM or ITSM link, or host-level blocking.

4.reason: LLM Firewall blocks prompt injection, PII and toxic responses inline. Response-side PII and hallucination controls not shown.
4.evidence: Stop toxic, biased or off-brand responses that alienate users and damage brand.
4.has: LLM Firewall inline, out-of-path API and OpenAI-compatible inline modes, plus client-side agents.
4.lacks: PII blocking shown on prompts only. No hallucination or harmful-code output filter.

5.reason: Compliance reporting covers ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act. Audit trail and auditor-ready reports.
5.evidence: Supported frameworks include: ISO 42001, NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF), EU AI Act
5.has: On-demand compliance reports for three frameworks, OWASP alignment, full agent audit trail.
5.lacks: No AIBOM export. Agent inventory only.

6.reason: No AI red teaming product. Radware publishes red teaming guidance and lists other vendors for it.
6.evidence: Searches: Radware AI red teaming product automated attack simulation, Radware LLM firewall red teaming. Only Cyberpedia guides found.
6.lacks: No attack library, multi-turn simulation or scheduled red team runs.

7.reason: MCP Tool Control allows or blocks tools per agent. Web Bot Auth verifies inbound external agents.
7.evidence: including agents that support Web Bot Auth (through cryptographic verification) and agents that do not
7.has: Per-agent MCP tool allow and block, plus Web Bot Auth checks on external agents.
7.lacks: No per-agent cryptographic identity for own agents. No API key or token governance.

8.reason: No model scanning, dataset scanning or AI SAST found. Radware lists such tools from other vendors.
8.evidence: Searches: Radware model scanning OR AI supply chain scanning OR AI SAST, Radware AI security posture shadow AI discovery.
8.lacks: No pickle or ONNX scanning, dataset PII scan or AI code scanning.

notes: Scope read: Radware Agentic AI Protection, LLM Firewall, MCP Server Protection and Agent Trust Management. LLM Firewall ships as part of Radware Cloud Application Protection Services. Evidence for modules 2 and 5 comes from the August 2026 Agentic AI Security and Governance solution brief. MCP Server Protection defends the customer's own MCP servers (protocol-aware WAF, DDoS) and maps MCP infrastructure. Agent Trust Management targets third-party agents that visit a customer's apps (login, checkout), not the customer's own agents. AI SOC Xpert is for Radware attack events, not AI app incidents. A third-party test cited by Radware rates its indirect prompt injection blocking at 95.7%. No acquisitions or rebrands found. Radware Cyberpedia pages describe red teaming, model scanning and SIEM integration only as generic guidance. Less sure: 1.2 (end-user devices plus client-side Claude Code agent counted as two surfaces), 4.1 (three integration modes from the brief, no browser extension named), 7.2 (per-agent MCP tool control counted as fine-grained).
